risk_if_not_implemented: Without Automated Audit Actions, the organization may fail to meet statutory, regulatory or contractual obligations, or be unable to demonstrate conformity when required. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Loss of Accountability / Attribution (R-AC-1), Loss of Investigative / Evidentiary Capability (R-IR-1), Undetected / Delayed Detection of Adverse Activity (R-SA-1), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Human Error (MT-9).

compensating_control_1.name: Session Audit
compensating_control_1.description:
Mechanisms exist to provide session audit capabilities that can: 
(1) Capture and log all content related to a user session; and
(2) Remotely view all content related to an established user session in real time.
compensating_control_1.justification: Session Audit (MON-18.1) provides detective monitoring capability that compensates for the absence of Automated Audit Actions (IAC-08.6) by identifying unauthorized, anomalous, or non-compliant activity that the primary control would have prevented. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Account Management
compensating_control_2.description:
Mechanisms exist to:
(1) Define authorized system account types;
(2) Define prohibited system account types; and
(3) Proactively govern individual, group, system, service, application, guest and temporary accounts.
compensating_control_2.justification: Account Management (IAC-08) provides access control enforcement that compensates for the absence of Automated Audit Actions (IAC-08.6) by restricting system and data access to authorized users through alternative identity and access mechanisms. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
